response.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS copies FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), avg_c AS (SELECT AVG(copies) AS avg_copies FROM counts) SELECT SUM(c.copies) AS total_copies, AVG(c.copies - a.avg_copies) AS avg_excess FROM counts c CROSS JOIN avg_c a WHERE c.copies > a.avg_copies

assumptions.assumption: Every inventory row is counted once, joined to its film via film_id. Ratings come from film.rating, and the average is taken over the 5 ratings that have inventory. The question does not settle whether ratings with no copies would count, but all 5 ratings have copies, so it makes no difference.
'Average amount by which their counts exceed the across-rating average' means the mean of (count - average) over the above-average ratings only, unrounded.
